subject: Service-name handoff & proxy trust anchor for private endpoints
messages:
From: Gina Park <gina.park@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint naming and TLS handoff (Acme)

Thanks for taking this on. Quick background: we are onboarding a set of private VPC endpoints for internal Acme services (svc1.acme.internal, svc2.acme.internal) and want Redwood to host the inference runtime in our VPC while we retain control of DNS and certificate keys. We need a concrete handshake plan for:

- DNS ownership assertions (how we delegate a subzone or provide TXT proof)
- Certs: options for customer-managed CA/HSM vs Redwood-provided certs
- TLS termination location: e.g., terminate at Acme egress proxy vs at Redwood sidecar inside our VPC
- SRV records and any special SNI mapping if wildcard certs are used

Attached is our current zone map and a short security requirements doc. Our security team will insist on HSM-based key custody if customer-managed certs are used. Can you outline steps and a timeline (we're targeting a 3-week ramp for the first tenant)?

Attachments: acme_zone_map_v2.pdf, acme_security_requirements.pdf

--
Gina Park
SRE Lead, Acme Cloud

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Gina Park <gina.park@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint naming and TLS handoff (Acme)

Gina — thanks, great context. High-level proposal and trade-offs below. I put a suggested minimal timeline at the end.

Option A — Delegated subzone + customer-managed CA (preferred for compliance)
- Acme delegates a read/write subzone (eg: redwood.acme.internal) to Redwood name servers for the endpoints we manage.
- Redwood runs an ACME client pointed at your internal ACME PKI or accepts signed CSRs you provide.
- Customer holds private keys in HSM; Redwood only receives certs and serves them from within the VPC sidecar.
- TLS termination happens at the Redwood sidecar; egress proxy still sees mTLS to your services if you request it.
Pros: meets HSM custody, clear ownership. Cons: requires BGP/DNS provisioning windows and a short zone cutover.

Option B — Redwood-managed wildcard + SNI mapping
- Redwood issues a wildcard cert (e.g., *.redwood.acme.internal) from our managed CA and serves via SNI mapping so each tenant sees their FQDN.
- Acme retains control of parent zone but provides TXT-based proof of ownership for issuance.
Pros: faster (no subzone delegation), easier rotation. Cons: customer keys cannot be HSM-backed on Redwood side.

Operational notes and asks (what we need from Acme)
- Which option do you prefer? If A, provide the delegated NS entries and contact for DNS ops. If B, confirm an acceptable TXT proof TTL and name prefix.
- OCSP stapling behavior: we will enable stapling by default; confirm your policy for stapled responses TTL and monitoring expectations.
- SRV record usage: if you plan to rely on SRV for service discovery, share the selector format so we can generate SRV entries in the delegated subzone.
- Canary window: propose a 48-hour canary in prod with an agreed rollback plan.

Timeline (estimate)
- Day 0–2: exchange zone map and decide option, produce CSR template if needed.
- Day 3–7: DNS delegation or TXT proof verification + initial cert issuance.
- Day 8–14: sidecar deployment, canary traffic, monitoring hooks.
- Day 15–21: rollout to full tenant fleet + final sign-off.

I'll loop Marissa on cert orchestration and Laura on DNS handoff details. If you prefer, we can sync for 30 minutes tomorrow to finalize.

Jordan Blake
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Gina Park <gina.park@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint naming and TLS handoff (Acme)

Thanks Jordan — that framing helps. A few clarifications from our side:

- Security will only sign off on Option A (delegated subzone) if we retain HSM keys. We can publish NS delegations within 48 hours once you provide the delegation template.
- We depend on SRV records for internal failover; format is: _redwood._tcp.svcX.redwood.acme.internal pointing to host:port weight/priority. Please ensure your sidecar accepts SRV-based routing rather than only A/AAAA + SNI.
- OCSP: our policy requires OCSP stapling and that stapled responses be refreshed at least every 12 hours.
- TTL: we prefer a 5-minute TTL on service records during canary and 1 hour after full rollout.

We attached our security requirements doc and a short checklist of CSR attributes we need to see (csr_requirements_checklist.xlsx). Legal also requested a short note that Redwood will not have key access under Option A — can you confirm in writing?

Attachments: csr_requirements_checklist.xlsx, acme_security_requirements.pdf

--
Gina Park
SRE Lead, Acme Cloud

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

On Wed, Oct 28, 2026 at 9:12 AM Gina Park <gina.park@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks for taking this on. Quick background: we are onboarding a set of private VPC endpoints for internal Acme services ...

Understood and confirmed: Redwood will not hold or have access to HSM private keys under Option A. Our role is "cert consumer" only — we accept customer-supplied cert bundles (PEM chain + private key kept in your HSM) or an externally-signed certificate you provide after CSR. We will store cert references and mount them into the runtime from the supplied artifact, but we will not perform key operations on your behalf. I'll have a short legal-friendly confirmation note drafted and send it as a follow-up.

Next steps I've scheduled:
- Marissa will run through the CSR attribute checklist with your security team tomorrow at 10:00 PT (I'll send calendar invite).
- Laura will publish a delegation template (NS records + glue suggestions) and the TXT proof format by EOD.
- We'll provision a canary environment and target 48 hours for the initial test; monitoring hooks (latency, cert errors, stapling failures) will be visible to both teams via the shared Grafana link in the JIRA.

Thanks — looping Marissa to take the cert ops work.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Redwood Inference
